findings.description: Decision 23 says "four of the five tools are still wired from their documentation rather than from a run anyone has watched (the matrix says which)," but docs/capability-matrix.md's own tally says three: "Three of five have never been run against. Codex, opencode and Cursor wiring is derived from their documentation... Vibe's has [been run against, via its own strict-mode loader test]." Claude Code is dogfooded and Vibe is explicitly tested, leaving only Codex, opencode, Cursor (3) as doc-only/unrun. Decision 23 cites the matrix as authority for this exact number, and the two disagree.
findings.body:
Decision 23 states: "four of the five tools are still wired from their documentation rather than from a run anyone has watched (the matrix says which)." But `docs/capability-matrix.md` explicitly counts three, not four: "Three of five have never been run against. Codex, opencode and Cursor wiring is derived from their documentation and has not been observed working. Vibe's has: its own loader accepts the emitted `hooks.toml` in strict mode, asserted by a test..." Claude Code is dogfooded daily and Vibe is tested via its strict-mode loader, so only Codex, opencode, and Cursor (3) are doc-only/unrun. Since decision 23 cites the matrix as the source for this exact count ("the matrix says which"), the two documents should agree, and currently don't.

findings.description: "...to run its own review tooling, so until something was published that pack shipped a red step." "Something" is a vague stand-in for "agent-init" — weaker than the parallel phrasing two lines below in decision 21's resolved-note ("until agent-init was published"). The missing comma after "published" also makes the clause momentarily garden-path.
